outcome: Risk factors for pediatric sleep-disordered breathing
cohort: 100 children who underwent adenoidectomy or adenotonsillectomy for sleep-disordered breathing
finding: A higher percentage of children with sleep-disordered breathing had mothers who smoked during pregnancy, while a smaller proportion habitually used a pacifier, and improved physical and academic scores were associated with reduced sleep-disordered breathing symptoms at follow-up.
mod_finding: A more significant proportion of patients undergoing adenotonsillectomy were observed to have a history of prematurity and cesarean birth.
